subject: bia
title: BIA.-----MULT.INFO.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-3 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One) anchoring the point Braxton states on this page: 'the collected forces of western culture have deliberately designed a reality perspective that retards the function of any affinity slant other than what it perceives as its own … only a selected area of information is made available to the public.' (C)BIA (the concept of bi-aitional) is crossed with (C)MULT-INFO (the concept of multi-information): the question is what bi-aitional produces when crossed with multi-information. Both subject and partner take the (c) prefix, marking that the crossing operates at the conceptual register (Braxton is analyzing the structural design, not just particular instances). PRIN-INFO (principle information) sits at the bend of the main line between subject and partner, and CULT-INFO-F (culture information focus) branches from it. From the stretch toward the partner, DYM-F (dynamic functionalism) drops down and carries C-INFO (composite information) and EXPM (expansionism); POST (postulation) also branches from that stretch and leads to C-ACT (composite activism), which carries AFI (affinity insight). From AFI the chain runs to EXT-FT (extended functionalism) and then to (R)INFO-DE (the reality of information degrees). Structural argument: bi-aitional crossed with multi-information is mediated through principle-information. The (c) prefix on both subject and partner is the structural claim: this is not about particular biases or particular information items, but about the *concept-level* design of western information filtering.
